summary: Destructor helper: when the flag byte at offset 8 is set, captures the pointer at offset 0 and, if non-null, calls FreeIfNonNull on it and then frees the captured block via FreeWrapper_7bcf. When the caller flag bit (a2 & 1) is set, additionally frees the object itself via FreeWrapper_7bcf. Returns this. Invoked by sub_495300 (0x00495300); the packet prelabel identifies it as a structural twin of UtilityFunction (004081e0).

local_names.a2: caller deletion-flag byte; bit 0 requests freeing this
local_names.v3: captured pointer from offset 0, freed after FreeIfNonNull

operations.description: Guard on the flag byte at offset 8: when zero, the inner data-cleanup path is skipped entirely.
Capture the pointer stored at offset 0 into v3.
Guard on the pointer at offset 0: when null, skip FreeIfNonNull and the FreeWrapper_7bcf of the captured block.
Call FreeIfNonNull on the pointer at offset 0 to release the object's resources.
Call FreeWrapper_7bcf on the captured block v3 to free its memory.
Guard on the caller flag (a2 & 1): when bit 0 is set, the object itself is freed.
Call FreeWrapper_7bcf on this when the caller requests deletion of the object itself.
Invoked by sub_495300 (0x00495300) as part of object teardown.

unresolved: The exact meaning of the flag byte at offset 8 (ownership/state marker) is not stated in the packet.

The packet prelabel clusters this with 004081e0 as a structural twin, but the callee sets differ (FreeIfNonNull + FreeWrapper_7bcf here versus MultiStageCleanupWithFree + FreeWrapper there) and this function additionally implements the a2 bit-0 self-free; class identity is not established.
The distinction between FreeIfNonNull and FreeWrapper_7bcf (a dedicated null-checking wrapper coexisting with a plain free wrapper) is not documented.
